cards.title: Staying hydrated
facts: Plain water is the best drink for everyday hydration.
You need more water in hot weather and during sport.
Energy drinks contain caffeine and are not meant for children.
do: Carry a water bottle
Sip through the day, not all at once
Drink more on hot days and after sport
dont: Don't use fizzy drinks to quench thirst
Don't have energy drinks

myths.statement: Energy drinks are a good way for kids to recover after sport.
myths.truth: They have lots of caffeine and sugar. Plain water is best after normal play.

quiz.q: You just played football for an hour on a hot afternoon. Best drink?
quiz.explanation: Plain water rehydrates best. Other drinks add a lot of sugar.

cards.reviewNote: Drafted from widely published guidance. Needs expert review before launch.

cards.title: Reading food labels
facts: Ingredients are listed from most to least.
'No added sugar' doesn't mean no sugar.
Nutrition values are often given per serving, not per pack.
do: Check the serving size first
Look at sugar and salt (sodium)
Read the first three ingredients
Check the expiry date
dont: Don't trust front-of-pack slogans alone
Don't assume 'baked' or 'multigrain' means healthy

myths.statement: A label saying 'no added sugar' means the food has no sugar.
myths.truth: It can still contain natural sugars, sometimes a lot. Check the sugar line.

myths.statement: Ingredients on a label are listed from the largest amount to the smallest.
myths.truth: The first ingredient is what the food contains most of.

quiz.q: On a food label, ingredients are listed…
quiz.explanation: The first ingredients make up most of the product.

situations: {At}, {name} is choosing a snack. One packet says 'Multigrain! Baked!' in big letters, but the label lists sugar and refined flour first. {relation} says the slogan means it's healthy.
scenario.question: How should {name} decide which snack is the better choice?

rubric.point: Read the ingredients list, not the slogan
rubric.note: Ingredients are listed from most to least.

rubric.point: Check sugar and salt per serving
Prefer fruit, nuts or roasted snacks as a better swap

cards.reviewNote: Drafted from widely published guidance. Needs expert review before launch.

cards.title: A balanced tiffin
facts: A balanced meal includes vegetables or fruit, whole grains and a protein.
Different coloured vegetables give different nutrients.
do: Fill half the plate with vegetables and fruit
Add a protein like dal, eggs, paneer, curd or sprouts
Choose whole grains like roti, brown rice or millets
Eat a rainbow of colours
dont: Don't skip breakfast
Don't make packaged snacks the main meal

myths.statement: Skipping breakfast helps you concentrate better at school.
myths.truth: Breakfast gives energy for the morning. Skipping it can make concentrating harder.

quiz.q: Which tiffin is the most balanced?
options: Roti, dal, cucumber and an apple
quiz.explanation: Grain + protein + vegetables + fruit = balanced.

cards.reviewNote: Drafted from widely published guidance. Needs expert review before launch.

cards.title: Food hygiene
facts: Washing hands with soap for 20 seconds removes most germs.
Cooked food left uncovered attracts flies and germs.
do: Wash hands with soap before eating
Wash fruits and vegetables
Keep cooked food covered
Refrigerate leftovers
dont: Don't eat food left uncovered for long
Don't share half-eaten food or bottles when sick

myths.statement: Rinsing hands with water alone is as good as washing with soap.
myths.truth: Soap helps lift germs off the skin. Wash for about 20 seconds.

quiz.q: How long should you wash hands with soap?
quiz.explanation: About 20 seconds, the time it takes to hum 'Happy Birthday' twice.

cards.reviewNote: Drafted from widely published guidance. Needs expert review before launch.

cards.title: Skipping breakfast impact and quick healthy fuel
facts: Skipping breakfast leaves blood glucose depleted after a 10-hour nocturnal fast.
Students who eat breakfast demonstrate higher memory retention and classroom focus.
do: Eat a balanced morning meal containing complex carbs and protein (poha, idli, eggs, or oatmeal)
Keep easy backup options ready: a banana, handful of roasted chana, or a boiled egg
Hydrate with a glass of water before leaving home
dont: Never replace breakfast with sugary sodas or packaged cream biscuits
Never attend morning exams on an empty stomach

myths.statement: Skipping breakfast helps students stay lean and active.
myths.truth: Skipping breakfast crashes morning metabolism and causes intense overeating of junk later.

quiz.q: Why does eating breakfast improve school exam performance?
options: It replenishes brain glucose needed for memory, focus, and quick thinking
quiz.explanation: Glucose from wholesome breakfast feeds the brain for alert cognitive performance.

situations: Running late for school at {at}, {name} wants to rush out without eating any breakfast.
scenario.question: What should {name} do for quick morning brain fuel?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Grab a quick healthy item like a banana, milk, or roasted chana
Do not skip breakfast entirely before school hours
Drink a glass of water before heading out

cards.title: Spotting hidden sugars in malt and 'health' drinks
facts: Many popular 'brown malt drinks' contain over 50% sugar by weight (sucrose, maltodextrin).
The WHO recommends keeping free sugars below 25 grams (about 5-6 teaspoons) per day.
do: Read the nutrition label: ingredients are listed in descending order by weight
Look for alias names for sugar: sucrose, liquid glucose, maltodextrin, high-fructose syrup
Enjoy plain milk or flavour with fresh cardamom, cinnamon, or cocoa powder instead
dont: Never believe front-of-pack claims like 'Energy Booster' without checking sugar grams
Never add multiple scoops of sugar to already-sweetened malt powders

myths.statement: Commercial chocolate malt powders are rich protein supplements for growing kids.
myths.truth: Most commercial malt mixes are primarily refined sugars and malt extract with minimal protein.

quiz.q: If 'Sugar' is the first or second ingredient on a food label, what does that mean?
options: Sugar makes up the largest proportion of that product
quiz.explanation: Ingredients must be listed in order of weight, from highest to lowest.

situations: In the supermarket at {at}, {name} looks at a health drink powder claiming 'Immunity & Growth'.
scenario.question: How can {name} verify what is really inside?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Turn to the back panel and check the Ingredients list
rubric.note: Reveals real composition and order of ingredients.

rubric.point: Check grams of added sugar per 100g serving
Do not rely solely on bold front-of-pack marketing claims

sources.name: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)

cards.title: Deconstruct junk food and fast food advertisements
facts: Food marketers use vibrant cartoon mascots, gaming partnerships, and free toys to target youth.
Ultra-processed foods are engineered to hit a 'bliss point' of sugar, salt, and fat that bypasses fullness.
do: Ask: 'What ingredients are they hiding behind this flashy celebration ad?'
Check the actual nutritional table rather than celebrity endorsement slogans
Understand that processed snacks are occasional treats, not everyday meal substitutes
dont: Never assume a snack is healthy just because a famous cricketer endorses it
Never replace fresh home-cooked meals with packaged snacks

myths.statement: Sports stars eat the exact packaged chips and soda they advertise on TV.
myths.truth: Professional athletes follow strict whole-food nutrition and rarely consume the ultra-processed products they endorse.

quiz.q: Why do junk food commercials feature energetic gaming and pop music?
options: To associate processed snacks with fun and coolness, bypassing nutrition scrutiny
quiz.explanation: Marketing targets emotions so consumers overlook high saturated fat and sodium levels.

situations: A viral TV ad at {at} claims a new crispy chip brand gives you 'Super Energy for Gaming'.
scenario.question: How should {name} critically evaluate this claim?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Recognize that the ad uses gaming themes to sell ultra-processed carbs
Check the nutrition label for sodium, trans fat, and refined palm oil
Treat chips as an occasional snack, not everyday study fuel

cards.title: Sodium and salt in instant noodles and packaged snacks
facts: A single packet of instant noodles often contains 70% to 100% of a student's daily sodium limit.
Excess sodium increases blood pressure, strains kidneys, and causes dehydration.
do: Check sodium mg on the label; ideal daily intake is under 2,000 mg (about 1 teaspoon of salt)
Use half the tastemaker seasoning packet and add boiled peas, carrots, or egg for balance
Enjoy instant noodles occasionally rather than as a daily after-school habit
dont: Never drink all the leftover salty noodle broth
Never add extra table salt to pre-seasoned chips and noodles

myths.statement: Instant noodles are just wheat flour and can be eaten daily for lunch.
myths.truth: Fried noodles are laden with palm oil, and seasoning packets are concentrated sodium bombs.

quiz.q: How much of your total daily sodium allowance can be in one packet of instant noodles?
options: Up to 70-100% of your entire recommended daily limit
quiz.explanation: One tastemaker sachet can exceed the recommended sodium intake for an entire day.

situations: Craving an after-school snack at {at}, {name} prepares a packet of instant noodles.
scenario.question: How can {name} make this snack healthier and lower in sodium?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Use half the tastemaker spice packet to cut salt in half
Toss in fresh vegetables (carrots, peas, spinach) or a boiled egg
rubric.note: Adds dietary fiber, vitamins, and protein.

rubric.point: Do not drink the remaining salty soup broth

cards.title: Eating local and seasonal fruits and vegetables
facts: Seasonal produce ripens naturally on plants, yielding maximum vitamin C and antioxidant levels.
Out-of-season produce is kept in cold storage for months and often treated with artificial ripening agents.
do: Eat seasonal fruits: mangoes/watermelons in summer; guavas/oranges in winter; papayas/bananas year-round
Choose local Indian fruits like amla, ber, jamun, and pomegranate for affordable rich nutrition
Wash all fruits thoroughly under running water before peeling or eating
dont: Never choose expensive imported apples over fresh local seasonal fruits
Never skip washing fruits before eating

myths.statement: Imported fruits with foreign stickers are much healthier than local Indian fruits.
myths.truth: Local Indian fruits like amla and guava contain 5 times more Vitamin C than imported apples.

quiz.q: Why is eating an amla (Indian gooseberry) or guava better than an expensive imported kiwi?
options: Local amla and guava pack far higher Vitamin C at a fraction of the cost and carbon footprint
quiz.explanation: Amla is one of nature's richest sources of Vitamin C, costing very little.

situations: Shopping for fruit with family at {at}, {name} sees costly imported berries alongside fresh local guavas.
scenario.question: Why is picking the local seasonal fruit the smarter choice?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Seasonal local guavas are fresher and richer in Vitamin C and fiber
Local produce supports nearby farmers and requires minimal transport emissions
Wash thoroughly with water before eating
rubric.note: Removes surface dust and handling residue.

cards.title: Powerhouse plant protein: Dal, sprouts, paneer and chana
facts: Proteins are the building blocks needed for muscle growth, tissue repair, and immune antibodies.
Combining grains and legumes (like rice + dal or roti + rajma) forms a complete amino acid profile.
do: Include a protein source in every meal: dal, chana, rajma, paneer, tofu, sprouts, or eggs
Sprout moong or chana at home to double their vitamin and digestive enzyme content
Snack on roasted peanuts or chana instead of fried potato chips
dont: Never rely solely on plain rice or bread without any lentils or legumes
Never take unverified gym protein powders without medical advice

myths.statement: Vegetarian diets cannot provide enough protein for growing school athletes.
myths.truth: Combining lentils, dairy, nuts, seeds, and sprouts provides abundant, high-quality complete protein.

quiz.q: What happens when you combine rice with dal or roti with rajma?
options: Their amino acids complement each other to form complete, high-quality protein
quiz.explanation: Grain + pulse combinations provide all nine essential amino acids.

situations: {name}'s school lunchbox at {at} contains only plain butter noodles.
scenario.question: How can {name} upgrade this meal to build strong muscles?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Add protein like paneer cubes, boiled eggs, tofu, or sprouts
rubric.note: Provides essential amino acids for growth.

rubric.point: Understand that protein keeps you satiated and alert through the afternoon
Snack on a small cup of roasted peanuts or moong sprouts

cards.title: Beating anemia: Iron-rich foods paired with Vitamin C
facts: Over 50% of Indian schoolchildren and teenagers have mild iron-deficiency anemia.
Vitamin C dramatically enhances the absorption of non-heme plant iron in the gut.
do: Eat iron-rich foods: palak (spinach), methi, beetroot, lentils, and jaggery in moderation
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over your dal and vegetables to boost iron uptake with Vitamin C
Cook in traditional cast-iron pans to naturally leach safe dietary iron into curries
dont: Never drink hot tea or coffee with meals (tannins block iron absorption)
Never ignore persistent symptoms of unusual fatigue, pale nails, and dizziness

myths.statement: Drinking a cup of chai right after eating dal and roti is good for digestion.
myths.truth: Chai tannins bind with dietary iron in your stomach, completely blocking its absorption.

quiz.q: What should you squeeze onto your dal to help your body absorb plant iron?
options: Fresh lemon juice (rich in Vitamin C)
quiz.explanation: Vitamin C converts plant iron into a chemical form easily absorbed by intestinal walls.

situations: During lunch at {at}, {name} notices palak dal on the table.
scenario.question: How can {name} maximize iron absorption from this green leafy meal?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Squeeze fresh lemon juice directly over the spinach dal
rubric.note: Vitamin C triples plant iron absorption.

rubric.point: Avoid drinking tea or caffeinated beverages right after the meal
rubric.keys: no tea|no coffee|avoid chai with food

rubric.point: Include iron-rich foods regularly to prevent fatigue and anemia
rubric.note: Keeps red blood cell hemoglobin high.

cards.title: Food allergies in friends and lunchbox etiquette
facts: Severe food allergies (nuts, eggs, dairy, shellfish) can trigger life-threatening anaphylaxis in minutes.
Even microscopic crumbs on shared spoons or lunchbox lids can induce an allergic reaction.
do: Always ask: 'Does anyone have food allergies?' before sharing homemade snacks
Never pressure friends to taste unfamiliar dishes if they express hesitation
Call a teacher and school nurse immediately if a friend experiences hives, lip swelling, or breathing difficulty
dont: Never tease or hide allergen ingredients in a friend's lunch as a prank
Never force a child with allergies to eat shared treats

myths.statement: If someone is allergic to peanuts, eating a tiny crumb will not hurt them.
myths.truth: Microscopic allergen traces can trigger severe airway constriction in sensitive individuals.

quiz.q: A friend at your lunch table says they have a severe peanut allergy. What is the respectful rule?
options: Force them to try peanut chikki
Never share peanut snacks and wash hands after eating
Tell them it's in their mind
quiz.explanation: Food allergies are serious medical conditions. Respect dietary boundaries completely.

situations: At lunchtime at {at}, {name} opens a box of peanut brittle (chikki) beside a classmate who has a peanut allergy.
scenario.question: What is the considerate, safe lunch etiquette for {name}?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Ask if having peanuts nearby is safe or eat at a considerate distance
rubric.note: Prevents accidental airborne or surface contamination.

rubric.point: Do not share utensils, spoons, or lunchboxes with the allergic friend
Know the symptoms of allergic reaction (facial swelling, hives, wheezing)

cards.title: Exam season brain fuel: Hydration, light meals and energy drinks
facts: Dehydration of just 2% significantly reduces mathematical calculation speed and attention span.
High-sugar energy drinks cause a sharp insulin spike followed by an exhausting brain crash.
do: Drink plain water, coconut water, or buttermilk regularly while studying
Eat light, frequent meals (fruits, nuts, curd, dal-chawal) to maintain steady glucose
Avoid heavy, oily deep-fried parathas or bhaturas right before morning exams
dont: Never consume high-caffeine energy cans to pull all-nighters
Never skip water during long study sessions

myths.statement: Canned energy drinks sharpen student memory for board exams.
myths.truth: Energy drinks cause heart palpitations, severe anxiety jitters, and a steep cognitive energy crash.

quiz.q: What drink provides the steadiest brain focus without causing jittery crashes during exam week?
options: Plain water, chaas (buttermilk) or coconut water
quiz.explanation: Hydration with clean water and electrolytes sustains cerebral circulation without spikes.

situations: Studying for important exams at {at}, {name} feels drowsy and considers buying a canned energy drink.
scenario.question: What is the wiser, scientifically sound brain-fuel choice?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Drink a glass of water, splash face with cool water, and take a 5-minute stretch break
rubric.note: Restores oxygen delivery to brain naturally.

rubric.point: Avoid high-caffeine energy drinks that trigger anxiety and crashes
rubric.keys: no energy drinks|avoid caffeine cans|no soda

rubric.point: Snack on a handful of almonds, walnuts, or an apple for clean energy

cards.title: Mindful eating: Chewing slowly and ditching mealtime screens
facts: It takes approximately 20 minutes for stomach satiety hormones (leptin) to signal fullness to the brain.
Eating while watching YouTube or TV distracts the brain, leading to subconscious 30% overeating.
do: Put phones and tablets away and switch off the television during meals
Chew each bite thoroughly to help saliva enzymes kickstart carbohydrate digestion
Pause halfway through your plate and check: 'Am I still genuinely hungry?'
dont: Never swallow meals in 3 minutes while glued to a mobile video
Never force yourself to finish overflowing portions when already comfortably full

myths.statement: Watching funny reels while eating helps you digest food faster.
myths.truth: Screen distraction blocks brain fullness signals, leading to overeating and acid indigestion.

quiz.q: Why does eating while watching videos cause indigestion and unintended weight gain?
options: Distraction prevents the brain from sensing fullness signals, causing unmeasured overeating
quiz.explanation: Mindless eating disconnects the brain from biological hunger and fullness cues.

situations: Sitting down for dinner at {at}, {name} instinctively props a phone against the water glass to watch reels.
scenario.question: How should {name} transform this into a healthy mindful meal?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Put the phone away and enjoy dinner with family without screens
rubric.note: Fosters mindful connection and satiety awareness.
rubric.keys: put phone away|no screens|turn off tv

rubric.point: Eat slowly, savoring textures, flavors, and chewing well
Listen to your stomach and stop eating when pleasantly satisfied

cards.title: Healthy balance during festival celebrations and feasts
facts: Festivals in India bring rich traditional sweets made of ghee, jaggery, milk, and nuts.
Labeling festive foods as 'evil' creates unhealthy guilt; balance and portion awareness work best.
do: Enjoy favorite festival sweets mindfully in small portions rather than bingeing
Prioritize homemade traditional treats over adulterated commercial sweets
Keep daily water intake high and eat plenty of fresh salad and fruit alongside festive meals
dont: Never skip regular meals to 'save room' for a massive binge of sweets
Never shame yourself or others for enjoying festival foods

myths.statement: Eating sweets during Diwali or Eid will immediately ruin your health permanently.
myths.truth: Traditional festive treats enjoyed in moderate portions as part of celebrations are perfectly healthy.

quiz.q: What is the best way to enjoy festival sweets without feeling sick or sluggish?
options: Eat 20 gulab jamuns in one sitting
Savor 1-2 pieces mindfully, stay hydrated, and balance with wholesome meals
quiz.explanation: Moderation, hydration, and positive family celebration preserve festive joy and health.

situations: It's festival day at {at}, and the dining table is filled with laddus, jalebis, and samosas.
scenario.question: How can {name} enjoy the festivities while taking good care of their body?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Choose favorite traditional treats and enjoy 1 or 2 pieces mindfully
rubric.note: Prevents sugar overload while partaking in festivities.

rubric.point: Drink plenty of water and eat regular fiber-rich vegetables
Do not skip normal meals or feel guilty about enjoying family traditions

sources.name: FSSAI Safe and Nutritious Food at Home

cards.title: Street food smarts: Hygiene checks and safe snacking
facts: Waterborne bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella, Vibrio) cause acute food poisoning and typhoid.
Uncovered cut fruits (papaya, watermelon) on roadside carts attract flies and vehicle exhaust fumes.
do: Choose stalls that serve freshly cooked, piping-hot food straight from the tava or kadhai
Ensure the vendor uses clean RO/filtered water, clean aprons, and covers food containers
Avoid pre-cut fruit platters or unpasteurized drinks mixed with crushed raw roadside ice
dont: Never drink roadside juices made with murky industrial block ice
Never eat food from stalls with flies buzzing over open ingredients

myths.statement: Roadside industrial block ice is made from purified RO water.
myths.truth: Block ice is often manufactured from unpotable water meant for chemical cooling, carrying typhoid microbes.

quiz.q: What is the safest type of street food to eat when snacking outdoors?
options: Pre-cut watermelon slices sitting out in the sun
Piping hot freshly steamed idlis or freshly fried samosas straight from hot oil
Open juice made with roadside block ice
quiz.explanation: High cooking heat kills bacteria instantly; freshly prepared hot foods are safest.

situations: Walking through a market at {at}, {name} and friends want to grab a quick street food snack.
scenario.question: What safety indicators should {name} check before ordering?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Check that the stall is clean, ingredients are covered, and vendor uses filtered water
Opt for freshly cooked piping hot dishes rather than pre-cut raw fruits
Avoid drinks made with crushed industrial block ice

sources.name: FSSAI Clean Street Food Hub Initiative

cards.title: Leftover food safety: Cooling, refrigerating and reheating
facts: The 'Danger Zone' for bacterial proliferation is between 5°C and 60°C.
Perishable cooked foods left at warm room temperature for over 2 hours multiply millions of bacteria.
do: Refrigerate leftover rice, dal, and curries within 2 hours of cooking
Store leftovers in covered clean containers and consume within 24 to 48 hours
Reheat leftovers thoroughly until steaming hot (above 74°C) before eating
dont: Never leave cooked food sitting out on the counter overnight
Never reheat the same batch of food multiple times

myths.statement: Smelling cooked food is an infallible way to tell if it has gone bad.
myths.truth: Many dangerous pathogenic bacteria (Staphylococcus, Salmonella) produce zero odor or taste changes.

quiz.q: Within how many hours must cooked food be refrigerated to stop bacterial growth?
quiz.explanation: After 2 hours at room temperature, bacterial populations double every 20 minutes.

situations: After dinner at {at}, a large pot of cooked chicken curry or paneer sits on the kitchen stove.
scenario.question: How should {name} handle these leftovers safely?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Allow it to cool slightly and place in refrigerator within 2 hours
rubric.note: Stops bacterial multiplication in the Danger Zone.

rubric.point: Store in a covered clean airtight container
rubric.note: Prevents contamination from fridge odors and moisture.

rubric.point: Reheat thoroughly until steaming hot throughout before eating tomorrow

sources.name: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food

cards.title: Reducing plate food waste at home and school
facts: Food waste rotting in landfills produces methane, a greenhouse gas 28 times more potent than CO2.
Taking smaller initial portions allows you to take seconds without throwing untouched food in the bin.
do: Serve smaller first portions on your plate; you can always ask for a second helping
Pack only the amount of lunch you know you will eat at school
Transform leftover rotis into healthy poha/rolls and leftover rice into fried rice
dont: Never heap mountains of food onto your plate that you cannot finish
Never throw away whole untouched fruits into the dustbin

myths.statement: Leaving food on your plate at restaurants shows that you come from a wealthy family.
myths.truth: Wasting food disrespects farmers' hard labor and exacerbates global environmental damage.

quiz.q: What is the simplest way to ensure zero food waste from your dinner plate?
options: Start with modest portions and take seconds only if still hungry
quiz.explanation: Portion control at serving time prevents untouched food ending up in trash bins.

situations: At the school canteen or dining hall at {at}, {name} is serving lunch from the buffet counter.
scenario.question: What plate habit ensures {name} leaves zero food waste?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Serve a modest first portion of rice, sabzi, and dal
rubric.note: Ensures you only take what you can eat.

rubric.point: Take second helpings only if still genuinely hungry
rubric.note: Adjusts intake to real hunger without waste.

rubric.point: Appreciate the farmers, water, and labor that produced the meal
rubric.note: Builds gratitude and respect for food.

cards.title: Building strong bones: Calcium, sunlight and Vitamin D
facts: Human bone density reaches its peak by age 20; adolescence is the critical window for bone building.
Without Vitamin D synthesized via sunlight, the body can absorb less than 15% of dietary calcium.
do: Consume calcium sources: curd (dahi), milk, ragi (finger millet), sesame seeds (til), and paneer
Spend 20-30 minutes outdoors in morning sunlight to allow skin to synthesize Vitamin D naturally
Engage in weight-bearing play like running, jumping rope, and dancing to strengthen bone matrix
dont: Never rely solely on calcium pills without consulting a doctor
Never spend all daylight hours indoors under artificial white lights

myths.statement: Only cow's milk contains calcium; non-milk drinkers cannot have strong bones.
myths.truth: Ragi (finger millet), sesame seeds, tofu, and dark leafy greens pack enormous calcium reserves.

quiz.q: Why is spending 20-30 minutes in morning outdoor sunlight crucial for your bones?
options: Sunlight triggers your skin to produce Vitamin D, which absorbs calcium into bones
quiz.explanation: Vitamin D is synthesized by UVB sunlight and acts as the gatekeeper for bone calcium absorption.

situations: {name} dislikes drinking plain cow's milk and worries about bone strength at {at}.
scenario.question: How can {name} build rock-solid bones through diet and lifestyle?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Eat non-dairy calcium rich foods like ragi, curd, sesame, and paneer
Get 20-30 minutes of natural outdoor sunlight daily for Vitamin D
Play weight-bearing sports like running, skipping, or football

sources.name: Indian Society for Bone and Mineral Research (ISBMR)

cards.title: Busting magic food fads, detox teas and crash diets
facts: The human liver and kidneys detoxify the bloodstream continuously; no tea or juice 'detoxes' you.
Severe calorie-restriction crash diets during teenage years stunt growth and damage hormonal health.
do: Recognize that no single superfood possesses magical healing powers; balance is everything
Trust whole home-cooked meals over expensive commercial detox supplements
Fuel your body with diverse food groups: grains, pulses, dairy/alternatives, vegetables, fruits, and healthy fats
dont: Never starve yourself on crash juice cleanses or unverified viral diets
Never eliminate whole food groups without certified medical advice

myths.statement: Drinking special green detox tea can melt away fat and flush all body toxins in 3 days.
myths.truth: Detox teas are marketing scams that act as harsh laxatives. Your liver cleans your body naturally.

quiz.q: What organs in your body already perform natural, scientifically proven detoxification 24/7?
quiz.explanation: The liver breaks down waste and the kidneys filter blood into urine continuously.

situations: A social media influencer at {at} urges teenagers to skip solid meals and drink an expensive 'Detox Cleanser'.
scenario.question: How should {name} react to this fad diet claim?
scenario.bubble: What is the safest move right now?

rubric.point: Recognize it as an unscientific marketing gimmick; the liver and kidneys detoxify naturally
Eat balanced, wholesome solid meals with plenty of water and fiber
Avoid dangerous crash diets that harm growing teen metabolism
